thread:
incident-bot: [ALERT] streaming-infer-prod p99 exceeded threshold (p99=6500ms) for 14m in region=us-west3  service=streaming-infer-prod  SLO p99=2000ms breached  fired at 2025-11-02T04:18:19Z :rotating_light:

sasha (oncall): ack. paging @jamal and @mike_ops. I'm seeing a sudden tail at ~04:15 across a handful of hosts in us-west3. No recent app deploys.

jamal: grabbing flamegraphs and trace snapshots now. p95 steady at ~780ms, but p99 has sharp jumps to 6-7s. Tail looks clustered to a few long-running streams.

ingrid: correlating infra metrics  stream_restart_count and stall_events spike tracked to us-west3-c. Suspect hardware-level instability. Nodes flagged: gpu-2042, gpu-2046, gpu-2051.

jamal: SSH into gpu-2042 logs. Posting kernel/runtime snippet below.

ingrid: log excerpt from gpu-2042:
```
[2025-11-02T04:16:02Z] kernel: GPU0: Correctable ECC error detected, count=6
[2025-11-02T04:16:18Z] nvml: power cap event; gpu temp=91C
[2025-11-02T04:16:21Z] runtime: perf throttling enabled; reduced clocks
[2025-11-02T04:16:25Z] service: stream stall; kv-cache lookup latency spike
```

jamal: CE bursts followed by thermal/power events. That'll create long outlier tokens for streams. @mike_ops can we divert new streams off these hosts and trigger quarantine?

mike_ops: initiating node isolation. Commands run:
```
kubectl label node/gpu-2042 incident=isolated --overwrite
kubectl cordon gpu-2042 && kubectl drain gpu-2042 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=20
```
Also toggling routing: bumping cpu-fallback to 70% and enabling reduced-precision model variants for streaming for 45m.

sasha (oncall): please capture counts: graceful session handoff vs killed sessions so CS can tally customer impact. Keep me posted on whether other nodes flip CE.

aly_cs: CS update  two customers reported noticeable lag during 04:14-04:22 window (accounts A-402 and B-991). They've been messaged with a short status note and offered priority follow-up.

hardware-bot: nvml-scan complete for us-west3 (past 90m) 
- gpu-2042: ce_total=14, t_max=92C
- gpu-2046: ce_total=8, t_max=90C
- gpu-2051: ce_total=2, t_max=77C
- remainder: ce<=1

jamal: recommend immediate quarantine of nodes with ce_total>5, schedule vendor RMA for gpu-2042 and gpu-2046. In-flight mitigation: shift traffic to healthy hosts and lower max_tokens for heavy streaming models by 30% for 3h to reduce sustained thermal pressure.

mike_ops: quarantine applied to gpu-2042 and gpu-2046, routing rules updated to avoid those nodes. Hardware ticket created: RMA-2025-2710  priority=P1  vendor=AccelParts  contact=escalations@accelparts.io. Attached nvml dumps and dmesg.

ingrid: after isolating nodes and routing adjustments p99 in region dropped to ~1.2s within ~80s. Stream-stall events decreased by ~85%. Monitoring for recurrence.

jamal: telemetry summary for post-incident: impacted traffic ~1.0% of region streaming traffic, peak affected streams ~180 concurrently. No sustained error-rate increase for HTTP endpoints. Classifying as partial degradation with localized hardware root cause.

sasha (oncall): handoff plan: I'm off shift in 25m. @jamal you will be incident lead until closure. Document action items: hardware RMA, driver/version audit across fleet, evaluate emergency driver patch if reproduces in staging, and draft customer incident note with exact impact window.

aly_cs: customers A-402 and B-991 confirmed receipt of messages and requested post-incident report. Offering SLA credit pending root cause.

jamal: action list captured:
- RMA and onsite diag for gpu-2042/gpu-2046 (mike_ops/hardware)
- Fleet driver audit and compare staging vs prod (ingrid)
- KV-cache integrity check for affected streams (jamal)
- Postmortem + customer impact write-up (sasha & aly_cs)

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE  status=mitigating  affected=partial_degradation  start=2025-11-02T04:18:19Z  update_time=2025-11-02T04:48:32Z

sasha (oncall): thanks all. We'll hold a follow-up review in #postmortems and link RMA-2025-2710. Close thread when RMAs complete and customer notes delivered. :white_check_mark:
